Issues.Title: Keep a block lambda body in an attribute with its tag when formatting Razor
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86427

When a C# attribute value spans lines, `VisitMultilineCSharpExpressionLiteral` takes the start tag's indentation (and one level for the start tag's brace, when the element causes indentation) off the continuation lines, because Roslyn adds it back structurally. Block-bodied lambdas were left out of that, since Roslyn keeps a block lambda's body where it is relative to the line the lambda starts on. That's right when the lambda starts on an attribute line of its own (`style="@(() =>` under the tag, the `DoesNotShiftRight` tests), but when it starts on the start tag's line the tag's indentation was counted twice:

- In a directive attribute (`<button @onclick="() =>`), the body moved right by the tag's indentation on every format, plus one more level when the element's content was on its own lines. That's the 4-column move noted in #86310: once WebTools has split the element, the IDE output of `MultilineBlockBodiedLambdaInDirectiveAttribute_MovesWithTag` had the body 4 columns right of the dotnet format output.
- In a component attribute (`<CheckBoxButton OnClick="() =>`), the `htmlIndentLevel--` for block lambdas cancelled it out at one level of nesting, so the body didn't move with the tag, and moved right when nested deeper.

The fix applies the start tag subtraction to block lambdas that start on the start tag's line, and skips the block-lambda `htmlIndentLevel--` for them. Lambdas that start on a later attribute line go through the existing path unchanged.

Tests (all `[WorkItem("https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/86427")]` except the first, in the shared `DocumentFormattingTest`, so each runs on both the cohost and the dotnet format path):
- `MultilineBlockBodiedLambdaInDirectiveAttribute_MovesWithTag`: the IDE `expected` now has the body at the same column as `dotNetFormatExpected`.
- `…InDirectiveAttribute_MovesWithTag_IndentByOne`, `_IndentByTwo` and `_Tabs`.
- `…InDirectiveAttribute_DoesNotMoveWhenFormatted` and `_ContentOnOwnLines_DoesNotMoveWhenFormatted`: already-formatted input, with the content on the tag's line and on its own lines.
- `MultilineBlockBodiedLambdaInComponentAttribute_MovesWithTag` and `_Nested_DoesNotMoveWhenFormatted`.

Results:
- **Mutation check:** with the generator change reverted, all 8 tests fail on the cohost path, and the 4 already-formatted and component tests fail on the dotnet format path (with the tag at column 0 the dotnet format output happened to be right). Reverting only the `htmlIndentLevel--` guard fails the two component tests.
- **macOS:** `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.UnitTests` passes, 456 of 456. The cohost formatting tests (`Microsoft.VisualStudioCode.RazorExtension.UnitTests`, `FullyQualifiedName~Formatting`) pass, 708 passed and 1 skipped. (Run before the `_IndentByOne` `htmlFormatted` fix below; after it, the 8 tests were re-run on the cohost path and pass.)

Issues.Title: Support multithreaded ProjectData slice writes
Issues.Body:
`WriteProjectDataSliceTask` currently resolves some paths and cache settings from process-global state, which is incorrect when MSBuild executes multiple projects concurrently in one process. Opt the writer into multithreaded execution and use its injected `TaskEnvironment` throughout the writer's helper chain.

- Flow an internal environment context through the source-linked cache, unsupported-marker, and donor-index helpers without introducing an MSBuild dependency into the reader library.
- Preserve the cache format, supplied output-path spelling, unchanged-content writes, project-adjacent cache preservation, and nonfatal cache-write failures. Direct construction and non-MT execution retain `TaskEnvironment.Fallback`.
- Add isolated-path/environment regressions and a real two-project MT smoke test. Enable `Microsoft.Build.TaskAuthoring.Analyzer`, with call-site suppressions documenting reviewed absolute-path flows. The analyzer uses `18.13.1-1.26560.4` because stable `18.13.0` is unavailable from the existing repository feeds; the MSBuild API baseline remains `18.7.1`.

## Composed-product evidence

Extracted `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Tasks.5.14.0-dev.nupkg` and used its `lib/net10.0` DLL, targets, and generated schema props. Set `CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonTargets` and `CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonCrossTargetingTargets` to the extracted targets. The fixture contains a single-target `net10.0` project and a referencing `net10.0;net11.0` project.

With SDK `11.0.100` / MSBuild `18.12.2.53018`, both commands exited `0`:

```powershell
dotnet msbuild Validation.slnx -t:ProjectDataBuild -p:DesignTimeBuild=true -p:BuildingProject=false -p:SkipCompilerExecution=true -p:EnableProjectDataInProjectFolder=true -m:2 -mt -nr:false '-warnaserror:MSB4286;MSB4287;MSB4288' '-bl:logs\authoritative-projectdata-mt-{}.binlog' -v:diag
dotnet msbuild Validation.slnx -t:Rebuild -p:EnableProjectDataOnBuild=true -p:EnableProjectDataInProjectFolder=true -m:2 -mt -nr:false '-warnaserror:MSB4286;MSB4287;MSB4288' '-bl:logs\normal-rebuild-mt-{}.binlog' -v:diag
```

Binlog inspection confirmed three writer invocations using the packaged assembly in-process, with no sentinel-CWD leaks. The generated caches contain the expected source and both target-framework slices. Thirteen packaged scenarios also cover unchanged-content writes, unusable staging-directory fallback, authoritative and non-authoritative empty command lines, marker recovery, stale-slice deletion, nonfatal write failures, non-MT execution, and an older supported host (SDK `10.0.404` / MSBuild `18.9.15.53019`). An intentional parent-build failure retained exit code `1` after the task successfully wrote its cache.

The packaged task DLL's SHA-256 is `88B29B88C26094B1774AF35EE9BB54ECAB82052DFAC1E1FEFB8EA1062295C1B3`.

## Known validation limitations

The locally installed pinned RC SDK imports its inbox ProjectData targets over the custom targets, so complete smoke validation used SDK `11.0.100`, which preserves the override. The new MT smoke test uses explicit task registration in non-SDK projects to avoid this ambiguity.

The full task suite had 470 passes and two independently reproduced existing Windows failures: `RunProcessWithTimeoutAsync_TerminatesHungProcessInsteadOfHanging` cannot resolve `ping` in its child process, and `AtomicWrite_CleansUpAndPreservesOutput_WhenReplacementFails` expects `IOException` while the original HEAD implementation throws `UnauthorizedAccessException`. These unrelated tests are unchanged.

Issues.Title: Format a multiline C# attribute value with a Razor transition as one expression
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86400
Fixes #86401

A C# attribute value that contains a Razor transition is split into several nodes around it. For `@onclick="() => Show(@x,` / `2)"` the value is `()`, ` =>`, ` Show(`, `@x`, `,` and a last literal that starts at the line break. `CSharpDocumentGenerator` visits each line by the node that starts it, so on the second line it only had that last literal. It carried forward an empty previous line, and Roslyn formatted `2);` as a statement of its own:

- with the transition on the first line (#86400), the `2)` line lost its alignment;
- with the transition on a middle line (#86401), that line went out as a C# statement of its own. Its changes overlapped the ones for the inline `@x`, and `SourceText.WithChanges` threw "The changes must not overlap" (the IDE logs "Formatting error. Abandoning further work").

**Fix:** a line that starts inside such a value, after its first line, is visited as the whole value. `VisitMultilineCSharpExpressionLiteral` now takes either a literal or the `MarkupTagHelperAttributeValueSyntax`, so Roslyn sees the same `() => Show(@x,` / `2);` it sees when the value is a single node (`@x` parses as a verbatim identifier). A value counts when its first child is a C# literal and it has more than one child. A string-typed component parameter starts with markup, so it's not affected. Single-node values go through the same code as before.

Tests, in the shared `DocumentFormattingTest`, so each runs through both the IDE and dotnet format hosts:
- #86400: the issue's repro (`_Unchanged`), and `MultilineLambdaWithTransitionInDirectiveAttribute_MovesWithTag` with all three attribute indent styles. Also `…WithExplicitExpression…` (`@(x + 1)`), `…InComponentAttribute…`, `…InBindAfterAttribute…`, and `MultilineMethodCallWithTransitionInBoundAttribute_MovesWithTag` (Legacy, `<cache enabled=…>`).
- #86401: the issue's repro (`_Unchanged`), `MultilineLambdaWithTransitionOnMiddleLineInDirectiveAttribute_MovesWithTag`, the same with `@(x + 1)`, with `@x` on the last line, in a component attribute, after a Razor comment, in a block-bodied lambda, and `MultilineMethodCallWithTransitionOnMiddleLineInBoundAttribute_MovesWithTag` (Legacy).

Results:
- **Mutation check:** without the fix, 14 of the 16 tests fail. The two Legacy tests pass either way: in a `.cshtml` tag helper attribute, `@x` stays inside the one C# literal, so that case was never broken. They're there as coverage.
- **macOS:** `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.UnitTests` passes, 473 of 473. The cohost formatting tests (`Microsoft.VisualStudioCode.RazorExtension.UnitTests`, `FullyQualifiedName~Formatting`) pass, 717 passed and 1 skipped.
- **Windows (net472, with the WebTools `htmlFormatted` validation):** passes, 903 passed and 1 skipped, on a [GitHub Actions run on my fork](https://github.com/Mpdreamz/roslyn/actions/runs/43188453100). The first run showed that WebTools keeps the content on the tag's line for the Legacy `<cache>` element, so those two tests now expect that on both paths.

Not covered, and already like this on `main`: a markup value (an unbound attribute, or a string component parameter) with `@x` that spans lines. Its continuation line moves to the tag's own column: with the tag at column 4, `<div title="Show(@x,` / `2)"` puts `2)"` at column 4 too. That's markup, not C#, and isn't touched here.

Issues.Title: Don't close an element twice when its end tag is split across lines in a Razor code block
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86396 Inside a code block, the parser includes the `>` of a split end tag in the end tag: ```razor @if (true) {
a

b

} ``` `Generate()` visits the end tag on the `` line, which emits a second one. The `>` line and everything after it in the block lost two levels of indentation. **Fix:** in `VisitEndTag`, a line that starts inside an end tag from an earlier line is now emitted as a comment. The exception is the case #86308 added: when the end tag doesn't start its own line, its close brace still goes on the first line it continues onto, and only if the element emitted an open brace. Before this change that check was missing as well, so a single-line element like `a` also emitted an unmatched close brace. If the `>` line ends a multiline template (`);`), the line keeps its indentation, because Roslyn doesn't indent a C# expression continuation there. **Tests** in `DocumentFormattingTest`, which run through both the cohost runner and the dotnet format runner: - `EndTagSplitAcrossLinesInIf` (the issue repro) and `EndTagSplitAcrossLinesInIf_Legacy` (`.cshtml`) - `NestedEndTagsSplitAcrossLinesInIf` - `EndTagSplitAcrossLinesInForeach` - `SingleLineElementEndTagSplitAcrossLinesInIf` - `EndTagSplitAcrossLinesClosesMultilineTemplate` (a `Render(@
…);` template in `@code`) WebTools joins `` into `
`, so only the dotnet format path (`dotNetFormatExpected`) shows the fix. All six fail without the change. The existing `EndTagSplitAcrossLines*` tests from #86308 still pass. - macOS: `DotNetFormat.UnitTests` 463 of 463 pass. I filed this against `9376c7a1aca`. That commit doesn't include #86308. #86308 emits the close brace for an end tag that isn't the first thing on its line, and that fixes this case too. On current `main` the issue's repro comes out unchanged on both the dotnet format and IDE paths, so this PR only adds tests to keep it that way.

Tests (in the shared `DocumentFormattingTest`, so each one runs on the cohost and the dotnet format paths):
- `ScriptEndTagSharesBodyLineDoesNotAffectFollowingContent`: the issue's repro, with the option on and off.
- `StyleEndTagSharesBodyLineDoesNotAffectFollowingContent`: the same shape with `<style>` and `}</style>`, with the option on and off.
- `ScriptEndTagSharesBodyLineDoesNotAffectFollowingContent_Legacy`: the repro in a `.cshtml` file, with the option on and off.
- `ComplexScriptEndTagSharesBodyLineInIfDoesNotAffectFollowingContent`: a complex script (it contains a Razor comment) inside `@if`, ending in `}</script>` and followed by more markup in the `@if` and after it.

Mutation check: with the close braces from #86308 disabled (`EmitCloseBracesForEndTagsLaterInLine` returning early), all 7 new cases fail on both paths.

Results:
- **macOS:** `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.UnitTests` passes 464 of 464. The cohost formatting tests pass, 708 passed and 1 skipped.

Not covered:
- **A non-complex script inside `@if`.** On the dotnet format path, a multi-line script inside `@if` has its body indented one level too deep, whatever the end tag looks like and with either option value. Html formatting is skipped there, so the generator reads the indentation from the source, and that includes the `@if` level. Each run adds another level. That's a separate bug, filed as #86429.

Issues.Title: Fix dotnet-new template samples test and dotnet-watch .slnx sharing violation
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
This PR combines two independent CI fixes so they can be reviewed and merged together. CI build [1678390](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1678390) passed with both changes applied.

- **Part 1** (first three commits, previously #57078): test the in-repo template engine samples instead of the published package. Fixes #57031.
- **Part 2** (last commit): release the generated `.slnx` write handle in `dotnet-watch` before building. Fixes #57065.

Fixes #57031
Fixes #57065

---

## Part 1: Test the in-repo template engine samples instead of the published package

`TemplateEngineSamplesTest` installed the latest *published* `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Samples` package, so publishing `11.0.100` (which drops `FSharp.NET.Sdk` from the F# sample) broke the checked-in `sample06 --language F#` snapshot.

The samples live in this repo (`documentation/TemplateEngine/Samples`), so the test now uses them directly instead of any package:

- `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Samples.csproj` marks its template content `CopyToOutputDirectory` (linked under `TemplateEngineSamples/`). The package layout is unchanged (verified the nupkg entries are identical).
- `dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.csproj` has a `ProjectReference` (`ReferenceOutputAssembly="false"`) to the samples project, so building the tests copies the templates into the test output.
- `TemplateEngineSamplesTest` installs the `TemplateEngineSamples` folder from its output directory.
- The F# snapshot is updated to the in-repo sample (plain `Microsoft.NET.Sdk`, no legacy package references).

Snapshots now always match the template content in the same commit.

Validated locally: all 16 `TemplateEngineSamplesTest` cases pass.

---

## Part 2: Release the generated `.slnx` write handle before building

### Root cause

Commit 2133b177c8f ("Create dotnet-watch solution files privately") changed `dotnet-watch` to keep the generated multi-project `.slnx` open with `FileAccess.ReadWrite` + `FileShare.Read` for the duration of the build. MSBuild's solution parser (`Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence`) opens the file with `File.OpenRead`, which requests `FileShare.Read`; Windows denies that open while another handle holds write access. From the Helix console of the failing runs:

```
aspire watch server ❌ ...\dotnet-watch-h42e2re5.vgl\1.slnx : error MSB4025: The project file could not be loaded. System.IO.IOException: The process cannot access the file '...\1.slnx' because it is being used by another process.
   at System.IO.File.OpenRead(String path)
   at Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence.Serializer.SingleFileSerializerBase`1...OpenAsync(...)
   at Microsoft.Build.Construction.SolutionFile.ParseUsingNewParser()
```

The initial build of the Aspire watch server failed, so `AspireLauncherIntegrationTests.ServerAndResources` waited for `Capabilities` output that never came until the test host was killed (hang dumps of `Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire` / `dotnet`). Any `dotnet watch` session that builds multiple projects through a generated solution on Windows hits the same build failure. The existing unit test masked the bug by reading with `FileShare.ReadWrite` instead of `File.OpenRead`.

### Fix

`TemporaryFileManager.Create` now takes a content writer: it writes through an exclusive handle, closes it, and then keeps only a read-only, `FileShare.Read` handle open until disposal. Readers using `File.OpenRead` succeed, while the file still can't be modified or deleted during the build (and stays in the owner-only private directory). `TemporaryFile` exposes `Path` instead of the underlying stream, so callers can't use a closed or read-only stream by mistake.

### Validation

- `TemporaryFileManagerTests` now reads via `File.OpenRead` (what MSBuild uses) and, on Windows, asserts that write access is still denied.
- Ran `TemporaryFileManagerTests` + `AspireLauncherIntegrationTests` locally on Windows against a rebuilt redist layout: 3/3 passed, and the server log shows `Build succeeded: ...\1.slnx`.

Note: #57066 (draft, Copilot coding agent) addresses the same `dotnet-watch` issue by reopening the handle at the call site; this PR instead makes the helper API safe by construction. Only one of the two should be merged.

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.1xx] Stabilize unrelated CI tests
Issues.Body:
🤖 Several release/10.0.1xx tests depend on asynchronous feed state or event reporting, causing unrelated CI failures that obscure product changes.

This change makes three test-only behaviors deterministic:

- Runs the template details command and expected-version lookup against the same explicit dotnet-public feed, using the product's NuGet metadata resolution path.
- Pins `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Samples` to `10.0.115`, matching this servicing branch and its checked-in snapshots.
- Waits for the dotnet-watch hot reload completion signal before asserting the remaining project-update event counts.

The NativeAOT tool failures from the investigated build are intentionally not worked around here. They are caused by incoherent regular and NativeAOT runtime package contents published under the same version and remain externally owned by dotnet/dotnet#5609.

Issues.Title: Harden container registry authentication redirects
Issues.Body:
## Problem

Authentication-realm requests currently follow redirects using custom redirect handling. Their redirect policy and authentication cache should be independent of ordinary registry operations.

## Description

Disable all redirects for authentication-realm requests while preserving normal registry redirects.

Replace the process-wide authentication cache with handler-local state to isolate clients using different credentials. Bound each request to one completed authentication acquisition, and restore authentication after retryable transport failures.

Issues.Title: SDK 11.0.100: SIGTERM sent to `dotnet <local-tool>` / `dotnet tool run` is not forwarded to the tool; the tool is orphaned (regression from 10.0.x, NativeAOT CLI path)
Issues.Body:
### Description

With SDK 11.0.100 on Linux, sending SIGTERM to `dotnet <toolcommand>` (or `dotnet tool run <toolcommand>`) kills the `dotnet` process at once. The tool process is never signalled. It is reparented to init/the subreaper and keeps running. With SDK 10.0.403, the same SIGTERM is forwarded to the tool by `ProcessReaper`, and both processes exit.

Setting `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0` with SDK 11.0.100 restores the SDK 10 behaviour.

Context: we hit this in a CLI that runs as a local tool and starts `dotnet watch` and a dev server, which process managers stop with SIGTERM.

### Environment

- Linux x64 (NixOS 26.11, kernel 7.3, glibc 2.44)
- SDK 11.0.100 (commit `297acf930f`), host/runtime 11.0.0. This is the official `dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-linux-x64.tar.gz`, SHA-512 verified against `release-metadata/11.0/releases.json`.
- SDK 10.0.403 (commit `5a2162bea6`), host/runtime 10.0.14, for comparison.

### Repro

`sigtool/sigtool.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <!-- lets the same package run on SDK 10 or on SDK 11 alone -->
    <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
    <PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>
    <ToolCommandName>sigtool</ToolCommandName>
    <PackageId>SigTool</PackageId>
    <Version>1.0.0</Version>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

`sigtool/Program.cs`:

```csharp
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;

string log = args.Length > 0 ? args[0] : "sigtool.log";
void Log(string s) => File.AppendAllText(log, $"{DateTime.UtcNow:HH:mm:ss.fff} {s}\n");

Log($"pid {Environment.ProcessId} ppid {File.ReadAllText("/proc/self/stat").Split(' ')[3]}");
using var term = PosixSignalRegistration.Create(PosixSignal.SIGTERM, _ => Log("got SIGTERM"));
using var intr = PosixSignalRegistration.Create(PosixSignal.SIGINT, _ => Log("got SIGINT"));
Thread.Sleep(Timeout.Infinite);
```

Pack it and install it as a local tool:

```sh
dotnet pack sigtool -c Release -o feed
mkdir use && cd use
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install SigTool --add-source ../feed
```

Start the tool with `dotnet` as session leader and send SIGTERM to the `dotnet` process only (from `use/`):

```sh
log=$PWD/sig.log; rm -f "$log"
setsid dotnet sigtool "$log" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
leader=$!
until [ -s "$log" ]; do sleep 0.1; done
tool=$(awk '/pid/{print $3; exit}' "$log")
ps -o pid=,ppid=,args= -g "$leader"
kill -TERM "$leader"; wait "$leader"; echo "dotnet exit status: $?"
sleep 3
if kill -0 "$tool" 2>/dev/null; then echo "tool ALIVE, ppid $(ps -o ppid= -p "$tool")"; else echo "tool exited"; fi
cat "$log"
kill -KILL "$tool" 2>/dev/null
```

Replace `dotnet sigtool` with `dotnet tool run sigtool` to check the other form.

### Expected (SDK 10.0.403)

`dotnet` forwards SIGTERM to the tool, and both exit. This happened in 3/3 runs of `dotnet sigtool` and in `dotnet tool run sigtool`:

```
dotnet exit status: 143
tool exited
19:05:16.390 pid 1001163 ppid 1001151
19:05:16.571 got SIGTERM
```

### Actual (SDK 11.0.100)

`dotnet` dies about 15 ms after the signal. The tool never receives SIGTERM, is reparented (here to `systemd --user`, the subreaper) and keeps running. This happened in 3/3 runs of `dotnet sigtool` and in `dotnet tool run sigtool`:

```
dotnet exit status: 143
tool ALIVE, ppid 1593        # systemd --user
19:07:54.527 pid 1003745 ppid 1003736
                              # no "got SIGTERM"
```

With `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0` and SDK 11.0.100, the tool logs `got SIGTERM` and exits, as with SDK 10.

`/proc/<dotnet pid>/status` shows that the SDK 11 `dotnet` process (which has `libdotnet-aot.so` mapped and no `libcoreclr.so`) does not catch SIGTERM:

| | `SigCgt` | SIGTERM (bit 15) caught? |
|---|---|---|
| SDK 10.0.403 `dotnet sigtool` | `00000003000344fa` | yes |
| SDK 11.0.100 `dotnet sigtool` | `0000000300030482` | no |

SIGINT is unaffected:

- SIGINT to the `dotnet` process alone: both SDKs ignore it, which is the intended `ProcessReaper` behaviour. Neither `dotnet` nor the tool exits, and the tool does not get the signal.
- SIGINT to the whole process group, as Ctrl+C does: on both SDKs the tool gets SIGINT, and `dotnet` exits with status 130.

So interactive Ctrl+C works. Only a signal aimed at the `dotnet` process is affected, such as `kill`, `systemctl stop`, an IDE's stop button, a CI step timeout or a container runtime.

### Regression

This is a regression from SDK 10.0.x. It looks like a reintroduction of dotnet/sdk#50965, which was fixed for SDK 10 by dotnet/sdk#50983, on the new NativeAOT entry point.

### Analysis (suspected cause)

This is based on reading the source at the 11.0.100 build commit (VMR `dotnet/dotnet@297acf930f`; `src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs`, `Program.cs` and `ProcessReaper.cs` are identical on `dotnet/sdk` `release/11.0.1xx`@`2b2b3b81a4`).

1. Since .NET 10 the runtime installs no default SIGTERM handler (dotnet/docs#46226). The managed CLI compensates in `Program.Main` with `PosixSignalRegistration.Create(PosixSignal.SIGTERM, _ => Environment.Exit(0))`. `Environment.Exit` raises `AppDomain.ProcessExit`, where `ProcessReaper` forwards SIGTERM to the child.
   - SDK 10: [`Program.cs#L37-L39`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/5a2162bea6845eabc1fc721624a43568c65db3b1/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet/Program.cs#L37-L39). The reaper subscribes to ProcessExit at [`ProcessReaper.cs#L51`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/5a2162bea6845eabc1fc721624a43568c65db3b1/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L51) and forwards at [`#L167`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/5a2162bea6845eabc1fc721624a43568c65db3b1/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L167).
   - SDK 11 managed CLI, still present: [`Program.cs#L78-L80`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet/Program.cs#L78-L80).
2. In SDK 11 the muxer calls `dotnet_execute` in `libdotnet-aot.so` ([`NativeEntryPoint.cs#L36`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L36)). Its own comment says that "the AOT host does not run Program.Main" ([`#L74-L75`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L74-L75)). Since dotnet/sdk#54810 / #54827, and on by default since #55144, external and local tool commands and `tool run` run inside that AOT process ([`#L239`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L239), [`#L393`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L393)). `NativeEntryPoint.cs` registers no `PosixSignalRegistration` for SIGTERM.
3. So `ProcessReaper` still subscribes to ProcessExit ([`ProcessReaper.cs#L151-L153`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L151-L153), forwarding at [`#L192`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L192)). But SIGTERM takes its OS default action, so the process ends without ProcessExit and the child is never signalled. This matches the missing SIGTERM bit in `SigCgt` above, and the fact that `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0`, which goes through the managed `Program.Main`, fixes it.

The open PR dotnet/sdk#56332 adds a `ProcessLifecycle` class with a SIGTERM registration that is used from `NativeEntryPoint`, and may fix this as a side effect. It is not merged or backported to `release/11.0.1xx`. A minimal fix for 11.0.1xx could be to register the same `SIGTERM → Environment.Exit(0)` handler at the start of `NativeEntryPoint.ExecuteCore`. Other in-process AOT paths that start a child with `ProcessReaper`, such as `AotRunCommand` for file-based apps, are probably affected the same way. We have not verified this.

### Impact

IDEs, CI systems, `systemd`, container runtimes and other process managers stop processes with SIGTERM to the PID they started. When that PID is `dotnet <local-tool>`, the tool — and whatever it started, such as `dotnet watch`, dev servers and application hosts — keeps running orphaned, holding ports and file locks. This is the same impact as dotnet/sdk#50965.

### Workarounds

- Set `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0`.
- In the tool, poll the parent PID and shut down when the `dotnet` process that started it is gone. This is what we do now.
- Send the signal to the whole process group instead of the `dotnet` PID.

Issues.Title: CA2007 does not report `await foreach` over `WithCancellation(...)` without `ConfigureAwait`
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

CA2007 reports an `await foreach` over an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` that has no `ConfigureAwait` call, but not one over `source.WithCancellation(cancellationToken)`. [`WithCancellation`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/313982dff3457c8291e8b88cd99785f6920319f0/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/Tasks/TaskAsyncEnumerableExtensions.cs#L36-L41) creates its `ConfiguredCancelableAsyncEnumerable<T>` with `continueOnCapturedContext: true`, so that loop resumes on the captured context just like the unconfigured one.

The analyzer [skips any `await foreach` whose collection is a `ConfiguredCancelableAsyncEnumerable<T>`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/88876b0c0b61b6e0ede17ac8e0ad8c95d3fc346b/src/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers/src/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers/Microsoft.CodeQuality.Analyzers/ApiDesignGuidelines/DoNotDirectlyAwaitATask.cs#L97-L99). `ConfigureAwait(bool)` and `WithCancellation(CancellationToken)` both return that type, so the type alone does not show whether the context was configured.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a class library with `dotnet new classlib --name Repro`, delete `Class1.cs`, and add this `.editorconfig` next to the project file:

```ini
root = true

[*.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.CA2007.severity = warning
```

Add `Sample.cs`:

```csharp
namespace Repro;

public static class Sample
{
    public static async Task RunAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<int> source, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await foreach (var item in source) { }
        await foreach (var item in source.WithCancellation(cancellationToken)) { }
        await foreach (var item in source.WithCancellation(cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false)) { }
    }
}
```

Run `dotnet build`.

### Expected behavior

CA2007 reports the first and second loops. The third loop calls `ConfigureAwait(false)`, so it is not reported.

### Actual behavior

CA2007 reports only the first loop:

```text
<repro>/Sample.cs(7,36): warning CA2007: Consider calling ConfigureAwait on the awaited task (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/quality-rules/ca2007)
```

### Is this a regression?

No. The `await foreach` check has skipped `ConfiguredCancelableAsyncEnumerable<T>` collections since dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#6683 added it.

### Are there any workarounds?

Write `.ConfigureAwait(false)` after `WithCancellation(...)` by hand. Nothing reports a loop where it is missing.

### dotnet --info output

Trimmed to the SDK, runtime environment, and host sections:

```console
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100
 Commit:            297acf930f
 Workload version:  11.0.100-manifests.08e30c08
 MSBuild version:   18.12.2-1.26529.118+297acf930

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     ubuntu
 OS Version:  26.10
 OS Platform: Linux
 RID:         linux-x64
 Base Path:   <dotnet-root>/sdk/11.0.100

Host:
  Version:      11.0.0
  Architecture: x64
  Commit:       297acf930f
```

### IDE version

None; reproduced with `dotnet build`.

### Other details

Telling the two calls apart means looking at the invocation chain that produced the collection, for example whether it contains a `ConfigureAwait` call, rather than at the collection's type.

dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#3703 is related: it asks for CA2007 to cover any type that has a `ConfigureAwait(bool)` method. This report is about a type the rule already handles.

_Drafted by Claude (Anthropic AI assistant)._

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Fix dotnet watch crash after switching target frameworks
Issues.Body:
A MAUI project can target both Windows and Android. Running it on Windows, then Android, then starting `dotnet watch` for Android can make the first C# edit crash with a `NullReferenceException` in Roslyn's `DefinitionMap.GetPreviousMethodHandle`.

Watch prepares compiler inputs for the selected target, but also loaded the other targets into Roslyn. If the earlier Windows build still matched the source, Roslyn tried to update Windows without complete compiler inputs, even though only Android was running.

This change passes the project instances from completed design-time builds to Roslyn, instead of every target in the project graph. It does not depend on C# compiler items, so VB and F# projects are kept too. Referenced projects targeting other frameworks are still included.

The regression test reproduces the crash without MAUI or a device: build another target first, start watch for the selected target, then edit a method. The control case skips the earlier build. All 18 focused tests pass, including source edits in VB and F#, dependencies, and project changes.

Related to https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/79898. This fixes the reproduced cross-target case; I have not confirmed whether it also fixes the empty-update case in that issue.

Issues.Title: Improve SDK task execution with multithreaded MSBuild
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Opt `EnsureHotReloadBrowserToolsKey`, `EnsureHotReloadWebSocketKey`, and `GenerateJSModuleManifest` into in-process multithreaded MSBuild execution, resolving filesystem operands through the injected task environment.
- Coordinate concurrent assets-file and targeting-pack cache initialization per retained engine-owned entry. Preserve build/process lifetimes, retry thrown initialization failures, avoid retaining task factories, and isolate cache entries across SDK assemblies/value types.
- Keep original path inputs for directory validation and key-write control flow. A shared resolver follows the actual host runtime and Framework legacy-path switch, rather than assuming a task's target TFM determines BCL behavior.
- Add concurrency, failure-retry, path-isolation, incrementality, invalid-input, and real-MSBuild mixed-runtime regression coverage. Document explicit redist SDK selection for contributor validation.

## Review follow-ups

Completed three review/fix passes covering cache ownership/concurrency, path/host compatibility, and final regression coverage.

The compatibility pass reproduced five failing cases for whitespace-only parent directories: argument-validation behavior changed and a key task could write the private half before failing. The final pass also reproduced a Framework task loaded by .NET MSBuild selecting the wrong validation policy. Both are fixed and covered by regression tests that failed before the fixes.

No dependency versions, generated output formats, or default non-MT command behavior are intentionally changed.

## Validation

Windows validation used the assembled `12.0.100-dev` redist with MSBuild `18.13.0-1.26528.111`, plus the installed .NET Framework MSBuild `18.13.0-1.26527.1`. Task assemblies were built for `net12.0` and `net472`; deployed DLL hashes were checked against build outputs.

```powershell
.\build.cmd -c Debug /bl:artifacts\log\mt-review-final.binlog

.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- `
  --project test\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests.csproj

.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- `
  --project test\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Tests\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Tests.csproj `
  --filter "FullyQualifiedName~EnsureHotReloadBrowserToolsKeyTest|FullyQualifiedName~GenerateJSModuleManifestMultiThreadingTest" `
  --repeat 2
```

- Full core task suite: **426 passed**.
- Focused SWA coverage: **35 passed**, twice.
- Configured ILLink smoke coverage: **3 passed**, including a successful linked publish and an expected failing publish.
- Composed-product matrix: **25 cases passed** across clean/incremental builds, explicit strict-mode sentinel probes, normal and suppressed execution, empty manifests, expected failure exits, publish exclusions, .NET Framework task/cache execution, and Framework task assemblies hosted by .NET MSBuild. Existing key/manifest bytes and timestamps stayed stable on no-op builds; generated JSON contained no sentinel paths and published output excluded key documents.

The existing pinned `Microsoft.Build.TaskAuthoring.Analyzer` was run without blanket suppressions. Its report-only `MSBuildTask0005` callback-provenance notes and `MSBuildTask0003` invalid-argument validation note were manually traced and covered by the compatibility/strict-mode cases; this is not presented as an analyzer-clean migration.

TRX and build/test binlogs are retained under `artifacts\log\test-runs\`; the composed matrix's commands, expected/actual exit codes, and logs were also retained with the session's reproduction fixture.

**Limitations:** Unix execution was not performed. These changes remove identified redundant work and enable in-process routing; no quantified overall build-time speedup is claimed.

Issues.Title: CA1508 false positive: Union switch in class gives warning
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

I have a union with a struct and a class, and when using the switch expression I get the CA1508 warning on the leg that uses the class. I believe this is incorrect, since the warning is not given for structs.
Using a full blown switch statement doesn't give this warning.

### Steps to reproduce

```C#
using System;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http;

internal record struct Any;
internal sealed record MyVersion(int Major, int Minor);
internal readonly union VersionOrAny(Any, MyVersion);

internal sealed class TestClass : IEquatable<Version>
{
    public VersionOrAny Version { get; init; }

    public bool Equals(Version? other)
    {
        if (other is null)
        {
            return false;
        }

        bool versionMatches = Version switch
        {
            Any => true,
            MyVersion value => other.Major == value.Major,
            _ => throw new UnreachableException()
        };

        return versionMatches;
    }
}

internal static class Program
{
    private static void Main()
    {
        TestClass test = new()
        {
            Version = new MyVersion(1, 1)
        };

        if (test.Equals(HttpVersion.Version10))
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("A different version should not match.");
        }
    }
}
```

### Expected behavior

No warning expected on the line saying `MyVersion version => other.Major == value.Major,`

### Actual behavior

CA1508 warning on the line saying `MyVersion version => other.Major == value.Major,`

### Is this a regression?

I can't say, older SDK's didn't support unions.

### Are there any workarounds?

A workaround would be to use a switch statement instead...

Issues.Title: Honor package source mapping in tool search and package completion
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Follow up on #55848 by applying package source mapping to tool search and package ID/version completion, so discovery results align with source selection when installing the tool or package.

- Filter tool search results by full package ID and originating source before expanding version details.
- Discover completion IDs on mapped enabled sources, then filter full returned IDs by origin rather than applying mapping to a partial stem. Preserve full-ID mapping for version completion.
- Honor explicit source overrides and reject additive-only sources when mapping is enabled.
- Pass selected project/file configuration context to completion, resolving relative sources against the invocation directory without MSBuild evaluation or project-count validation. Existing multi-project directories support completion; missing targets return no suggestions.
- Isolate completion source validation, resource discovery, and query failures per feed so healthy suggestions survive, while retaining HTTP opt-in requirements and default source validation for other callers.

Package acquisition, SDK installation, cache, signature policy, templates, and workload paths are unchanged. Completion uses directory-based NuGet configuration, not arbitrary MSBuild-evaluated restore properties. Defensive handling of versionless template catalog entries remains deferred.

## Validation

Windows x64:
- Managed CLI build passed with zero warnings/errors.
- 67 focused CLI tests, 7 source-configuration tests, and 5 actual NativeAOT tests passed, with no failures or skips.
- Native tests include concise/detailed managed/native tool-search parity over a controlled local feed.
- Regression coverage includes mapping precedence and origin filtering, overrides, HTTP opt-in and feed isolation, inherited configuration clearing, relative targets, and mid-line completion.
- Product/redist assembly hashes match; `git diff --check` passes.

Native product library increased by 1 KiB in the follow-up build; existing IL3053 dependency warnings remain, with no added suppressions. Linux/macOS and external authenticated-feed execution were not exercised.

Issues.Title: dotnetup: verify system root architecture from the dotnet executable header
Issues.Body:
## Problem

dotnetup decides a system root's architecture from where it was registered, not from what is on disk:

- **Windows:** the `HKLM\SOFTWARE\dotnet\Setup\InstalledVersions\{arch}` subkey that points at the folder ([`WindowsPathHelper.GetProgramFilesDotnetRoot`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/dnup/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/WindowsPathHelper.cs)).
- **macOS:** the `/etc/dotnet/install_location_{arch}` file, or the OS architecture for the arch-less file and default locations ([`DotnetEnvironmentManager.AddMacOSRoots`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/dnup/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/DotnetEnvironmentManager.cs)).
- **Linux:** the OS architecture.

This matches how the .NET host finds its root, and it is correct for every layout the official installers produce. A registration that contradicts the files is still trusted, for example `InstalledVersions\x64\InstallLocation` pointing at an x86 install.

Before #56935, discovery loaded each root's `hostfxr`, and a mismatched root failed to load with `BadImageFormatException`, so it was skipped (with a warning). Discovery now walks folders without loading native code, so a mislabeled root is listed as dotnetup's own architecture.

## Impact

Low; nothing breaks:

- `dotnetup init` shows the folder as the system install location and labels its channels with dotnetup's architecture.
- Migration requests those channels for dotnetup's own root and architecture, so the user gets native builds; nothing is copied from the mislabeled folder.
- Layout conflict checks only look at dotnetup's own root and manifest, so there are no false conflicts.

The only failure would be a migrated channel with no build for dotnetup's architecture, which reports `NoMatchingReleaseFileForPlatform` and is classified as a Product error even though the machine is misconfigured.

## Proposal

Read the architecture from the root's `dotnet` executable header before trusting a root's label, and skip or warn when it does not match the expected architecture:

- **PE (`dotnet.exe`):** `MZ` header, `e_lfanew` at `0x3C`, `PE\0\0` signature, then the COFF `Machine` field: `0x14C` x86, `0x8664` x64, `0xAA64` arm64.
- **Mach-O / ELF:** the CPU type in the Mach-O header and `e_machine` in the ELF header.

This reads a few bytes and does not load or execute anything.

The VS Code .NET Install Tool already does this for PE, Mach-O, and ELF, and is a good starting point: [`ExecutableArchitectureDetector.ts`](https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-dotnet-runtime/blob/9c0a49f62da1b2d7190129c2e60e2dbe20aab2c9/vscode-dotnet-runtime-library/src/Utils/ExecutableArchitectureDetector.ts).

## Considerations

- A root can be partial and lack the muxer; keep the registration's label in that case.
- macOS universal binaries (fat Mach-O) need handling, or should keep the registration's label.
- The same check could apply to dotnetup's own roots and to `--architecture` support (#55083).
- Decide whether a mismatch is skipped silently, warned about, or recorded in telemetry.

Related: #56935, #55083, #55350.

Issues.Title: Select issue triage assignees deterministically
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Issue triage has assigned every recent `Area-NuGet` issue to `@zivkan`. The prompt asked the agent to load-balance with `web-fetch`, but the Copilot CLI never exposes `web_fetch` to the model, even with `copilot-sdk: true`. The agent then fell back to "choose randomly" and picked the same name every time. In two runs, its reasoning named `@nkolev92` while the tool call assigned `@zivkan`.

This PR moves owner selection into code. A read-only `select-assignee` MCP script resolves the `CODEOWNERS` section, expands teams from a membership snapshot, counts each candidate's open issues created in the past week, and picks the lowest count. Ties are broken with `crypto.randomInt`. The agent calls the script once and assigns exactly the login it returns.

## Evidence

| dotnet/sdk run | Issue | Assigned |
|---|---|---|
| [42011849728](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/42011849728) | #56943 | zivkan |
| [42618174003](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/42618174003) | #57002 | zivkan |
| [43016080908](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/43016080908) | #57062 | zivkan |
| [43018542973](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/43018542973) | #57063 | zivkan |

Each run's `agent` artifact (`sandbox/agent/logs/process-*.log`) shows that the model's tool list had no `web_fetch` and that the model reasoned it "can't fetch pages".

## Changes

- `.github/scripts/issue-triage-assignee.js`: selection logic. A pre-agent step copies it, its snapshot, and `CODEOWNERS` to `${{ runner.temp }}/issue-triage-private`, and a JavaScript `mcp-scripts` tool loads it from that copy. It uses the read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and reads only the issue search API; the area input is validated and never interpolated into a query.
- `.github/scripts/issue-triage-team-snapshot.json`: team snapshot moved out of the prompt, unchanged.
- `issue-triage.md`: removes `web-fetch:` and `copilot-sdk: true`, allows `mcpscripts:*`, and replaces the CODEOWNERS matching and load-balancing instructions with "call `select_assignee` and use its result". The lock file was regenerated with gh-aw v1.0.1 on Linux.
- `.github/scripts/issue-triage-assignee.test.js`: unit tests, run by the existing helper-tests workflow. One test checks that every CODEOWNERS and snapshot team is listed in `safe-outputs.mentions.allowed`.

## Security

- **Token scope.** The tool receives the agent job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which has `contents: read` and `issues: read`. The workflow already passes the same token to the MCP gateway, the GitHub CLI proxy, and safe outputs. Only the host-side MCP scripts server receives it; the agent sandbox does not. The agent can already make the same reads through `gh`.
- **No agent-writable code.** The agent sandbox mounts the workspace read-write and has the `write` tool. Loading the selector from the checkout would therefore let a prompt-injected agent rewrite it and run code on the runner host. The selector and its inputs are staged under `runner.temp`, which the sandbox does not mount, before the agent starts. `stale-reference-interpret.md` uses the same pattern. The tool is a JavaScript handler, not a `run:` handler: a `run:` handler would resolve `node` through `PATH`, which includes the agent-writable `~/.local/bin`.
- **Regression tests.** Tests check that staging runs after checkout and before the agent, and that the tool never references `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`.

## Behavior changes to review

- **ILLink/ReadyToRun section boundary.** The old prompt's rule ("stop at the next comment") contradicted its own ILLink example, which included `@dotnet/dotnet-cli` below an in-section comment. A section now ends at a comment that follows a blank line, or at the next `Area-*` heading. This matches the example.
- **Load metric.** The count no longer filters on `label:untriaged`. Triage removes that label when it assigns someone, so the old query counted roughly zero for everyone.
- **No assignability preflight.** The old prompt mentioned one but never defined it. Stale snapshot members will fail at assignment, as they do today.

## Validation

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.4xx] Fix native MTP target framework and runtime display
Issues.Body:
## Description

Backport of #57035 (merge commit `0a0943c49529c7902ce706d6fc713310f0644728`) to `release/10.0.4xx`.

Relates to microsoft/testfx#7066.

Separate a test module's actual target framework from its executing runtime. Project/solution runs prefer the evaluated `TargetFramework`; module-only runs can use optional handshake field 21; otherwise the target remains unknown. Required field 2 remains runtime information, with this branch's existing protocol 1.0 and required-field behavior unchanged.

This is a release-branch adaptation, not a wholesale cherry-pick: retain the older reporter, xUnit tests, constructor/call signatures, retry accounting and summary behavior. Add a required sixth-argument runtime overload rather than importing newer attempt/settings APIs. Preserve identity through start, results, completion, discovery, summary and both progress renderers; narrow cursor progress drops secondary runtime information before target/architecture or the filename. The new field is also named `TargetFramework` in existing handshake traces.

The controller-capability post-processing correction from the source PR is inapplicable because `ArtifactPostProcessingManager` does not exist here. No newer heartbeat, error-recap, post-processing, retry/settings or test-framework infrastructure is imported. This branch has no vendored-files manifest; the shared formatter is attributed to the immutable TestFX source commit instead. All 13 XLF updates were generated with `UpdateXlf`.

## Customer Impact

A genuine `net472` test running on .NET Framework 4.8.1 now displays `(net472|x64, runtime: net481)`, rather than falsely identifying its target as `(net481|x64)`. A known matching target stays compact, for example `(net481|x64)`. An older module-only peer without target metadata displays `(x64, runtime: net481)` without inferring a target from the runtime or output directory.

Full target TFMs and platform suffixes remain visible. Modern runtime servicing patches and target platform suffixes are ignored only when comparing target/runtime equality; .NET Framework `net48`/`net481` and `net471`/`net472` remain distinct. The architecture is the actual executing process architecture.

## Regression?

The introduction commit has not been established. The untouched release-branch base `3d90ce145149e0369f594f1289f27528c98d2f21` reproduces the incorrect identity in the branch-built SDK, including passing, failing and zero-result runs. This PR does not attribute the bug to a particular introducing change.

## Risk

Low code risk: limited to identity metadata and presentation, with no selection, result-count, command, exit-code or dependency-policy changes. The corrected module-only output for old peers is an intentional user-visible change and may affect consumers parsing the previous incorrect identity.

Branch dependencies remain unchanged and coherent: `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` **2.1.0-preview.25571.1** and `MSTest` **4.1.0-preview.25571.1**, both from TestFX `43e592148ac1c7916908477bdffcf2a345affa6d`. Optional target metadata from a newer peer is not required for project/solution correctness or old-peer compatibility.

The default full build has an independently reproduced baseline blocker: installer `finalizer.csproj` restores `Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler` 10.0.12 and fails with **NU1903**, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9. Managed redist and CLI/test builds passed. Native-AOT finalizer/installer validation is not claimed; no audit/analyzer diagnostics were suppressed and no package versions were changed. Servicing approval is not claimed.

## Testing

**73/73 focused xUnit tests passed**, with zero failures, errors or skips, against the committed source. Coverage includes formatter comparison, old/new/absent metadata, required runtime fields, controller-before-host ordering, stable retry identity/counts, cursor widths/long filenames, simple progress, discovery/summary surfaces, real project/glob runs, legacy retry and no-handshake failures.

**25/25 composed product cases passed** using the branch-built **10.0.403** shipping SDK layout: **14** new-peer cases and **11** cases with the unchanged 2.1 peer. These are real MTP executions, not helper mocks or an installed newer CLI. Each run uses an explicit isolated consumer CWD, SDK/root/resolver settings and separate package caches. Parent exit codes and summary counts are checked against independently generated target/runtime/process/selected/executed/outcome XML; multi-module runs also verify both artifacts and aggregate counts.

| Observable path | Verified result |
|---|---|
| `net472` project, old/new peer | `(net472|x64, runtime: net481)`; exit 0, selected/executed/passed 1 |
| `net472` module, new peer | `(net472|x64, runtime: net481)`; exit 0, executed/passed 1 |
| `net472` module, old peer | `(x64, runtime: net481)`; exit 0, executed/passed 1 |
| Known matching `net481` and `net10.0` targets | Compact target/architecture identity; exit 0 |
| `net8.0` major roll-forward | Target remains `net8.0`, runtime is `net10.0`; actual runtime .NET 10.0.12 |
| Genuinely absent assembly target metadata | Module target unknown; evaluated project target still preferred |
| Actual x86 .NET Framework process | `(net472|x86, runtime: net481)`; XML confirms X86 and one passed test |
| Deliberate failure, old/new peer | Exit 2; selected/executed/failed 1; failure diagnostic preserved |
| Zero-result run, old/new peer | Exit 8; selected/executed/total 0 |
| `net472` + `net481`, old/new peer | Exit 0; two independent execution artifacts; total/succeeded 2 |

Five additional **clean-base red-phase** cases retain the original incorrect identity with independently verified exits/outcomes; the matching `net481` control stays compact. They are source-built evidence, not the separate installed-SDK baseline.

The new-peer test package `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.3.0.0-dev.framework7066.final1` was used only in an isolated local feed/cache. Its nuspec source stamp is `c2b618b17ef3ecbf46054cde3785476673ff9f63` and SHA-256 is `E476C77337E7AF644D03D475F36DCECFE8307CB66BB36058316F6BA6FCAF8139`; it is not a shipping dependency upgrade. Existing traces explicitly retain `Framework: .NET Framework 4.8.10008.0` and `TargetFramework: net472`.

Build/test commands (PowerShell; binary logs retained):

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Layout\redist\redist.csproj -c Debug -m -p:PublishAot=false -p:SkipBuildingInstallers=true -p:SkipUsingCrossgen=true -bl:baseline-managed-layout.binlog --nologo -v:minimal
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe msbuild src\Cli\dotnet\dotnet.csproj -t:UpdateXlf -p:Configuration=Debug -bl:localization.binlog -nologo -v:minimal
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj -c Debug --no-restore -m -p:PublishAot=false -bl:commit-stamped-build.binlog --nologo -v:minimal
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe exec artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet.Tests.dll -method '*TestFrameworkDisplayTests.*' -method '*TerminalTestReporterTests.*' -method '*TestApplicationHandlerTests.*' -method '*TestProgressStateTests.*' -method '*GivenDotnetTestReportsTargetFramework.*' -method '*GivenDotnetTestBuildsAndRunsTestBasedOnGlobbingFilter.*' -method '*GivenDotnetTestRunsConsoleAppWithoutHandshake.*' -method '*RunTestProjectWithWithRetryFeature_ShouldSucceed*' -xml commit-tests.xml -nologo
```

The committed CLI and its 13 existing satellite assemblies were deployed into `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet\sdk\10.0.403` before the final test and composed-product runs. The source map identifies the exact commit below.

<details>
<summary>Retained result/provenance manifest</summary>

```json
{
  "commit": "a75067deadfb8e11faaefa2b7af1545f66f5cbce",
  "parent": "3d90ce145149e0369f594f1289f27528c98d2f21",
  "sdk": "10.0.403",
  "baselineCliSha256": "37D66A9D2EB183385E2DAAB8072EBF5AD686819D2ABA2A21A1218C48175BC5E6",
  "testedCliSha256": "D7BD3987EC20F8EFB8AA35C88DA423A10EC0CECB0E6BFB1F07AF70604621350C",
  "focusedTests": { "total": 73, "passed": 73, "failed": 0, "skipped": 0 },
  "composedCases": { "newPeer": 14, "shippingPeer": 11, "cleanBaseRed": 5 },
  "generatedXlfFiles": 13,
  "nativeFinalizerValidated": false,
  "diagnosticsSuppressed": false
}
```

Full evidence retains the xUnit XML/log, per-case stdout/stderr/commands/traces and independently emitted execution XML, old/new/baseline summaries, package hashes/source stamps, source map and build/localization binlogs.

</details>

Issues.Title: .NET SDK 11.0.100 Static Web Assets net472 tasks ship an incompatible Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces version
Issues.Body: ### Describe the bug When a `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` project is built with .NET SDK 11.0.100 using full-framework Visual Studio MSBuild, the Static Web Assets task fails to load `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces, Version=10.0.0.10`. The same project builds with core-hosted MSBuild (`dotnet build`). ### Steps to reproduce Install .NET SDK 11.0.100 and use a Visual Studio Developer Command Prompt whose full-framework MSBuild supports that SDK. global.json: ```json { "sdk": { "version": "11.0.100", "rollForward": "disable" } } ``` Repro.csproj: ```xml net11.0 enable ``` Program.cs: ```cs var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); var app = builder.Build(); app.MapGet("/", () => "Hello"); app.Run(); ``` From that directory, verify dotnet --version reports 11.0.100, then run: ```ps1 msbuild Repro.csproj /restore /v:minimal ``` ### Expected behavior The project builds successfully, as it does with: ``` dotnet build Repro.csproj ``` ### Actual behavior Full-framework MSBuild fails in Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.targets while generating the Static Web Assets manifest: ``` error : FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces, Version=10.0.0.10, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' or one of its dependencies. at Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.Tasks.StaticWebAssetsManifest.ComputeManifestHash() ``` Another observed path throws during initialization of `StaticWebAssetEndpointResponseHeader` through `StaticWebAssetsJsonSerializerContext`. ### Is this a regression? Yes. Our builds were fine under .NET SDK 10.0.402 ### Are there any workarounds? Copilot came up with a couple different workarounds: #### Surgical assembly resolver ```xml { var requestedAssembly = new AssemblyName(args.Name); if (requestedAssembly.Name == "Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces" && requestedAssembly.Version == new Version(10, 0, 0, 10)) { return Assembly.LoadFrom(AssemblyPath); } return null; }; ]]> <_StaticWebAssetsBclAsyncInterfacesAssembly>$([System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath('$(StaticWebAssetsSdkDirectoryRoot)\..\..\DotnetTools\dotnet-format\BuildHost-net472\Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces.dll')) ``` #### A bunch of UsingTask elements ```xml <_StaticWebAssetsNetTasksAssembly>$(NetCoreRoot)sdk\$(NETCoreSdkVersion)\Sdks\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets\tasks\net472\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Tasks.dll ``` ### dotnet --info output ```console ``` ### IDE version _No response_ ### Other details **Payload analysis** For full-framework MSBuild, `Sdk.StaticWebAssets.CurrentVersion.targets` selects the tasks/net472 task payload. In SDK 11.0.100 that directory contains: * `System.Text.Json.dll` assembly version 10.0.0.10, which references `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces` version 10.0.0.10. * Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces.dll assembly version 11.0.0.0. * No Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces version 10.0.0.10 and no binding redirect for it. Because this is a strong-named dependency loaded by .NET Framework MSBuild, version 11.0.0.0 does not satisfy the request for 10.0.0.10. Interestingly, the SDK contains the required 10.0.0.10 assembly elsewhere at `DotnetTools/dotnet-format/BuildHost-net472/Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces.dll`; copying/resolving that assembly makes the task run. The tasks/net472 directory should ship a consistent dependency closure, for example by including Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces 10.0.0.10 or by rebuilding/shipping dependencies that consistently reference version 11.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118741 | ASP.NET Core Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. know if I am affected? Check the deployed runtime and application package versions against the affected ranges above. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? Install the applicable runtime or update each independently referenced package to the fixed version above. After updating standalone packages, rebuild and redeploy affected applications, including framework-dependent applications; restarting alone does not replace app-local packages. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Body: > **Announcement consolidated:** See the [November 2026 ASP.NET Core security announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/504) and [shared feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70467). This original CVE post is retained for existing links. Closing it does not withdraw the advisory or its remediation guidance. ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. SignalR Redis scale-out can mishandle case-mismatched group removal and leave subscriptions in a state that permits persistent resource amplification and denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70467 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-401 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The tables list affected version ranges and fixed package versions.
